summary: Mason County state fire tower built 1936, staffed to 1956, replaced by South Mountain, destroyed 1961; one footing reported, and the site is a logging landing on Green Diamond land.

facts.design: 40-foot timber tower with a 14x14 cab (L-4 cab per firelookout.com)
facts.status_note: Tower destroyed in 1961; later logging covered the site in crushed rock; one footing reported, and a 2022 visitor found no recognizable artifacts

access.note: On Green Diamond tree farm land: no pass or permit required; motorized access through a gate only during autumn hunting season; non-motorized visits year-round when forestry work is not posted (2022 write-up)

visit.trail_note: Willhite lists 3 miles from a parking spot on the 800 line; roads off that line are usually signed to mean no motor vehicles; the 2022 write-up gives 3.4 to 6.6 mile round trips from different starting points

events.note: 40-foot treated timber tower with a 14x14 cab built by the state
Aircraft Warning Service station Charlie 2-1, run jointly by Simpson Logging Company and the state; afterward the state kept the site as a fire detection point
Mrs. Roe Franklin transferred from the Simpson lookout to the new South Mountain lookout
South Mountain lookout announced to replace the Simpson lookout
firelookout.com and Willhite say destroyed; register says removed that year
Register says the tower was removed in 1961
Around the 1980s the site became a logging landing; the site has since been covered in crushed rock

notes_for_editor: Elevation disagrees: 1,000 ft (1956 Daily Chronicle item quoted by Forest Lookouts), 1,200 ft (firelookout.com; the record's 365.8 m is 1,200 ft), 1,240 ft (Willhite and the 2022 write-up). Story gives all three. Destruction versus removal in 1961 is also disputed (firelookout.com and Willhite say destroyed; the register says removed); both kept. The 2022 write-up says the tower sat partway down the southern slope of Simpson Peak, not on the summit. Current condition is disputed: Willhite saw one half-buried footing; the 2022 visitor found no recognizable artifacts but did not search the salal thoroughly. Access is 'public' from the brief's 'unknown', based on the single 2022 blog's account of Green Diamond gate rules; gate rules may have changed, so a human should re-check the Green Diamond public-access page the post links to before publication. Willhite's 3-mile distance is not stated as one-way or round trip. The search snippet's South Mountain 1976 cab-removal claim was not read on a page and is not used. The brief's height is not in the sources and is left out of facts. Research used 1 WebSearch and 6 page reads, within budget.
